conviction_note: The two measurements agree in sign but differ in size (findings sum -2.5, scaled -0.84). The guide was struck on 13 July at ~$3.20/gal all-in for Q3 and ~$3.00 for Q4. Delta's own July-to-actual fuel gap (+$0.46/gal in Q3) and its $4.25 Q4 assumption imply a mechanical Q4/FY reset of roughly 7-9 margin points before fare recapture. That pulls the reaction negative. Three things hold p_up near the middle at 43: management pre-warned twice in its August and September traffic releases; the stock already sits 29.5% off its high; and the name bought its last two prints (Q2 +2.3% despite a fuel overrun, Q4'25 about +9%).
bar: Company guide from the Q2 release (6-K Ex.99.1, 2026-07-13, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001561861/000119312526302103/d112634dex991.htm): 3Q26 revenue $1.59-1.62bn (+12-14%), adj. EBITDAR margin 26.5-29.5%, operating margin 14-17%, ASMs +0.5-1.5%, fuel ~$3.20/gal all-in, MXN 17.5. 4Q26: revenue $1.64-1.68bn, op margin 15.5-18.5%, fuel ~$3.00/gal, MXN 17.6. FY26: revenue $6.05-6.12bn, op margin 11-13%. The EPS consensus is UNSOURCED/disputed: Tickflow $0.24 (2 analysts, as of 2026-08-06), Benzinga $0.43, TipRanks $0.61 with no analysts behind it (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mx:aero/earnings). So the reported-quarter findings are capped small, and print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue against the guide midpoint of $1.605bn.

Curved Trading showed 0.88M, 3.3 DTC and a 3.3% borrow fee as of 2026-06-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/aero/). Benzinga shows about 0.7% of float. Not a crowded short, so the negative findings are not shrunk for squeeze risk. findings.finding: Q3 fuel very likely ran well above the guide's ~$3.20/gal all-in assumption. Delta, guiding off the same mid-July curve, assumed $3.15 and realised $3.61 (+$0.46, >$500M over its July guide, and that is net of a 13c refinery benefit Aeromexico does not have). Gulf Coast jet hit $4.705 in mid-September and $4.40 on Sep-29. At ~117.5M gallons a quarter (444.7M litres in Q2), each +$0.10/gal is about $12M, roughly 0.75 points of Q3 operating margin. A $0.5-0.6 overrun is $60-75M gross, or $15-20M net after the 75% recapture Aeromexico achieved in Q2. That points to operating margin at or below the 14% low end, against a revenue line likely above the $1.62bn top end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sweep says the baseline history is traffic 6-Ks, not prints. Confirmed prints: Q2 2026 (2026-07-13 amc), where fuel expense came in $30M above guide and the result was called 'in line', moved +2.29% next session per the baseline row. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026) moved about +9% per StockTitan. Delta's Q3 miss on the same fuel cause sold about -3% on 2026-10-09, and AERO fell 1.33% that day in sympathy.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Aeromexico itself said fuel was 'higher than anticipated' (August traffic release, 2026-09-03) and 'a more challenging cost environment than anticipated' (September traffic release, 2026-10-06), but never quantified it or changed the guide. If the size were fully priced, the stock would have fallen through the September fuel spike. Instead it is +1.25% over 20 days, and the 'Strong Buy'/$28-46 targets and $0.24-0.61 EPS estimates are stale from before August.
findings.independence: Company pre-warning in its own traffic release: https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results (2026-10-06). Gulf Coast spot: https://www.globalair.com/articles/aviation-fuel-spotlight-oil-is-flowing-but-jet-a-didnt-get-the-memo?id=12728. Q3 assumption and gallons: the 6-K Ex.99.1 of 2026-07-13. Shares Delta's evidence with the guidance finding below; the Q3 quarter and the Q4 guide are separate lines.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide assumed ~$3.00/gal all-in and MXN 17.6. Delta now guides Q4 at ~$4.25/gal, and USD/MXN is ~18.3-18.4 in mid-October. On ~120M Q4 gallons the fuel gap alone is ~$120-150M, about 7-9 points of the 15.5-18.5% Q4 operating-margin guide before recapture, or roughly 2-3 points net at a 75% recapture. A reset of the Q4 and FY (11-13% op margin) outlook, or a withdrawal, is very likely on the 10-20 call. Delta cut FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 on the same cause.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April Aeromexico guided Q2 down on fuel (Q1 print, 2026-04-21 amc). The next-session move is not sourced; the baseline's 04-23 row is -4.92% but may be a traffic day. Delta's 2026-10-09 FY cut on fuel traded about -3%. United's July Q3 guide below the Street on fuel fell 2-5% after hours.
findings.why_not_priced: The $3.00 Q4 assumption is in the company's only standing guide and has never been withdrawn. Its scale is not on any wire. If the market had priced a 2-3 point net cut to Q4 margin plus FX, AERO would have traded down with Delta's guide cut beyond its -1.3% sympathy move and would not be +1.25% over 20 days. Partly offset: the stock is already 29.5% below its high, and the CEO flagged fuel twice, so some de-rating has happened.
findings.independence: Company Q4 assumptions: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001561861/000119312526302103/d112634dex991.htm (2026-07-13). FX at 18.38 on Oct-16: https://www.publimetro.com.mx/noticias/2026/10/16/precio-del-dolar-hoy-peso-mexicano-se-mantiene-en-1838-ante-presion-inflacionaria-en-ee-uu/. Delta's Q4 $4.25 assumption is a peer proxy, not Aeromexico's own number. It shares the Delta document with the Q3 fuel finding.

findings.finding: Demand and capacity sit inside or above the Q3 guide. Q3 ASMs by month were July -1.5%, August +2.3% and September +3.4%, about +1.3% for the quarter against the +0.5-1.5% guide. RPMs were -1.9%, +2.9% and +3.6%. Load factor was 88.0%, 89.7% (+0.6pp) and 87.1% (+0.1pp). September international RPMs grew +6.6% on +6.3% capacity, and management called forward bookings 'healthy'. Together with US airfares up 23% y/y and Delta's +14% yield, this supports revenue at or above the $1.62bn top end through fuel recapture.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record revenue (+12.6%, inside guide) came with a +2.29% next-session move. Q4 2025 record revenue came with about +9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Traffic is public, so volume is priced. Yield (TRASM) is not published monthly, and the recapture rate in a quarter where fuel rose late is the unknown part. The market sees a revenue beat as the cost of fuel, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: July: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/03/3337941/0/en/Aeroméxico-July-2026-Traffic-Results.html. August: https://finviz.com/news/388703/aeromexico-august-2026-traffic-results. Peer pricing: Delta's yield +14% (beancount.io 2026-10-10). Volaris September: international RPMs +14.2%, domestic -3.8% (https://finviz.com/news/399322/volaris-reports-september-2026-traffic-results-load-factor-of-84).

findings.finding: The Eleventh Circuit vacated DOT's order terminating the Delta-Aeromexico JV's antitrust immunity on 2026-08-20. This is the first print since then, so management can restate network and JV economics for Q4 and 2027 rather than planning around an unwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AERO rose +3.31% (08-21) and +4.79% (08-24) around the ruling per the baseline rows; those are not prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock rose about 8% over the two sessions after the ruling. What remains is any quantified commentary on the call (JV revenue, the status of DOT rehearing), which the market has not seen.

findings.finding: The ASPA pilots' union rejected a 3.2% wage offer and extended its strike deadline by 45 days from 2026-09-30, to about mid-November, while flight attendants settled at 4.1%. The call will likely be asked about labour cost and strike risk to Q4 guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to labour news for this listing.
findings.why_not_priced: It is Spanish-language domestic press with no US wire coverage. The strike date itself falls after the window, so only the call commentary and any labour-cost line in a new guide count here.

findings.finding: The peso gave back its year-to-date gains in September. USD/MXN rose 7.4% in the month to Oct-12 to about 18.2-18.4, against the guide's 17.5 (Q3) and 17.6 (Q4). On the Q2 release's own description, a strong peso lifted USD revenue and raised costs, so the reversal trims USD revenue for Q4 and may produce an FX remeasurement in Q3. The net effect on operating margin is ambiguous.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction on the FX line. In Q2 management attributed both revenue support and cost pressure to the strong peso.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. Q4 FX is the second assumption in the standing guide that has moved, and the stock has not traded on it visibly.
findings.independence: Proxy only. https://www.liderempresarial.com/el-peso-mexicano-culmina-la-semana-con-perdida-cual-es-el-precio-del-dolar-hoy/ says September erased the year's peso gains.

outside_window.finding: The ordinary shareholders' meeting to approve a $100M-a-year share repurchase ceiling is reportedly set for 2026-10-26, after the exit window. The program was first announced 2026-08-24. The previous program was suspended.
The pilots' strike deadline extended 45 days from 2026-09-30 falls around mid-November. The strike or settlement itself resolves after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: No October 2026 sell-side preview or price-target change for AERO; the latest dated actions are Jefferies Hold $20 and JPM $26.50, both June 2026.
No 2026 secondary or follow-on offering, and no Apollo or holder sales. The IPO lock-up has long expired and Delta's 4-year lock-up still holds.
No intra-quarter guidance revision 6-K between 2026-07-13 and 2026-10-19; the fuel wording appears only in the traffic releases.
No published Q3 average for Mexican ASA/Pemex turbosina or for the INEGI airfare sub-index for September 2026.
United's Q3 2026 results were not found as published, so Delta is the only peer print available.
No usable option skew or implied move: the chain is unusable.

baseline_tension: The baseline gives no skew and no implied move. The flat 20-day run-up (+1.25%) through a September fuel spike and a peer guide cut suggests the reset is not fully in the price, which supports the negative lean. The 29.5% drawdown from the high and a record of buying fuel-hit prints cut against it, so p_up stays at 43 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 / core 'bar disputed' and 'inside what the company told the market': the Q3 fuel finding went from -1.5 to -1.0. The EPS consensus is unsourced, and management pre-warned twice that fuel was above plan.
Rule 1 / reaction function: this name bought its last two prints, including the fuel-hit Q2 (+2.29%). The Q4 guidance finding went from -2.0 to -1.8, and p_up moved from 42 to 43.
Rule 5: the demand finding rests on public traffic and a peer yield proxy for pricing, so it went from +0.8 to +0.6. The FX finding stays small (-0.3) and is labelled a proxy.

'Rebuild the base rate from confirmed releases': abs_move_pct 6.0 rests on confirmed print reactions (Q2 +2.29%, Q4'25 about +9%), the 46.6% realised vol and a likely guidance change, not on the traffic-day history. Left unchanged.
Rule 7: short interest was checked (0.7% of float, 3.2 DTC). It is not crowded, so no squeeze shrink was applied to the negatives.
